steps: Single bracket: multiply each inside term by the outside term
Double brackets: use FOIL or a grid, then collect the middle terms
Squared bracket: (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b², keep the 2ab term
Difference of two squares: (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b²
method_card.title: How to Expand Brackets
method_card.content:
Single bracket: multiply every term inside by the term outside: \(a(b + c) = ab + ac\).

Double brackets use FOIL (First, Outer, Inner, Last): \((x + a)(x + b) = x^2 + (a+b)x + ab\). Collect the two middle terms.

Squaring: \((x + a)^2 = x^2 + 2ax + a^2\). Do not drop the middle term.

Difference of two squares: \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\); the middle terms cancel.

For triple brackets, expand two first, then multiply by the third.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Single brackets: multiply the outside term by each term inside, keeping every sign.
problem_bank.silver_description: Two brackets with FOIL: multiply every term in the first by every term in the second, then collect the middle terms.
problem_bank.gold_description: Harder expansions: squared brackets, difference of two squares and triple brackets. Keep every term.

bronze.title: Bronze: one bracket
steps: A single bracket like \(4(x + 3)\) means 4 times everything inside. Multiply the outside term by each term in the bracket.
Keep the signs. A negative outside, or a minus inside, flips the sign of that term: \(4 × 3 = 12\) but \(-4 × 3 = -12\).
One bracket has nothing to collect. If two brackets are added, expand both, then combine the like terms.

silver.title: Silver: two brackets
steps: Two brackets multiplied, like \((x + 3)(x + 5)\), need FOIL: First, Outer, Inner, Last. Every term in the first multiplies every term in the second.
That gives four terms. The two middle ones are like terms, so add them: \(5x + 3x = 8x\).
Watch the signs. A minus inside a bracket travels through every product it touches.

gold.title: Gold: squares, triples and two-square differences
steps: Squaring is FOIL with itself: \((x + 6)^2 = x^2 + 12x + 36\). The middle term \(2 × 6 × x\) is the one people drop.
Difference of two squares: \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\). The middle terms cancel, so no \(x\) term is left.
For triple brackets, expand two first, then multiply the result by the third, collecting like terms at each stage.

opener.label: Before any algebra
opener.display: A rectangle 4 tall is split into a part 10 wide and a part 3 wide.

steps.say: Area is just width × height, and a split rectangle's total is its parts added up. Take the left block first: 4 tall, 10 wide.
Add the two parts to get the whole rectangle.

Multiplying the whole width at once, 4 × 13, also gives 52. Splitting then adding matches multiplying. Now swap the 10 for \(x\) and the SAME rule expands the bracket: \(4(x + 3) = 4x + 12\). The 4 multiplies each part inside. That is all expanding a bracket is.
The 5 multiplies each term inside, one at a time.
So \(5(x + 4) = 5x + 20\). Check it by putting x = 1 into both forms.
steps.hint: Work out the bracket first, then multiply.

steps.done: Both give 25, so the expansion is right.
